candidates.summary: round 2's dotted-alias-key fix covers static aliases only: a realm (GnowebPath) alias keyed /license.md or /Terms still gets canonical and og:url https://gno.land//license.md
candidates.failure_scenario: -aliases '/license.md=/r/gnoland/pages:p/a' (or /Terms): realmAlias sets sp.url = ParseFromURL(&requested), which parses /license.md as File under Path "/"; canonicalURL encodes it as //license.md, so the indexed page names as canonical a URL that answers 400
candidates.evidence: /license.md status=200 robots="index, follow" canonical="https://gno.land//license.md" og:url="https://gno.land//license.md"; /Terms canonical="https://gno.land//Terms"; //license.md status=400 title="Invalid path - gno.land"; /about canonical="https://gno.land/about" (control). Author's thread reply scopes the fix: 'static pages are now named by their alias key'

candidates.summary: aliasTargets keys an alias by its target's path and args and drops the target's $ view, so an alias to a $source view becomes the canonical of the bare realm page
candidates.failure_scenario: -aliases '/s=/r/gnoland/pages$source' (accepted by parseAliases, and /s serves the source view): aliasOf["/r/gnoland/pages"] = "/s", so /r/gnoland/pages, index follow, names https://gno.land/s canonical and search engines fold the realm page into its source view; a target with ?query keys the same way and points the bare page at an alias that does not serve
candidates.verify_by: go test ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb -run TestB5_ViewAliasTakesRealmCanonical -v -count=1 with the artifact copied in
candidates.evidence: /s status=200 robots="index, follow" canonical="https://gno.land/s"; /s serves the same body as /r/gnoland/pages$source; /r/gnoland/pages status=200 robots="index, follow" canonical="https://gno.land/s" og:url="https://gno.land/s"
